presentation_summary: Woman in her 40s with type 2 diabetes mellitus was hospitalized for scheduled cerebral revascularization for moyamoya disease.
Home medications included empagliflozin, metformin, pioglitazone, atorvastatin, and levothyroxine; antihyperglycemics were held on admission.
Postoperatively she developed stroke and then progressive metabolic acidosis during the next 24 hours despite near-normal glucose values.
The acidosis included pH nadir 7.01, PCO2 11.5 mmHg, anion gap rising to 27, serum CO2 less than 5 mmol/L, normal lactate, beta-hydroxybutyrate 7.7 mmol/L, urine glucose 2+, and urine ketones 4+.
Diagnosis and response to dextrose plus insulin infusion are retained as confirmatory/non-ranking.

risk_context.source_text_value: empagliflozin; last dose at least 18 hours before surgery
scheduled cerebral revascularization; nutritional support had not yet been started due to dysphagia/aspiration concerns
acute left anterior cerebral infarct postoperatively

observations.source_text_value: home medications included empagliflozin; last dose at least 18 hours before surgery
scheduled surgery and no nutritional support during the first 48 postoperative hours
glucose 149 mg/dL on POD1; glucose 160-167 mg/dL on POD2
anion gap increased to a peak level of 27
serum CO2 <5 mmol/L on POD2; POD1 serum CO2 14 mmol/L

confirmatory_findings.finding: Final attribution to euglycemic DKA related to SGLT2 inhibitor therapy
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: A diagnosis of euglycemic diabetic ketoacidosis, presumably related to SGLT2 inhibitor therapy, was made.

confirmatory_findings.finding: Anion gap closure after dextrose and insulin drips
confirmatory_findings.source_text_value: dextrose and insulin drips, leading to closure of the anion gap acidosis

outcome.source_text_value: Due to the severity of brain injury resulting from her stroke, comfort measures were instituted, after which the patient died.

quality_warnings: SGLT2 exposure, surgery, fasting, and stroke stress are context/risk factors, not disease-name qualifiers.
Near-normal glucose is retained as rankable evidence to pressure the manifold to cover euglycemic DKA.
Treatment response and final attribution are confirmatory/non-ranking.
